summary.short: Sets cybersecurity risk-management requirements (Annex) and significant-incident criteria for listed DNS, cloud, data centre, online platform, managed service, trust service and other relevant entities under Directive (EU) 2022/2555; binding in all Member States, in force 20 days after OJ publication.
summary.long: Implements Article 21(2) and Article 23(3) of Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2) for listed relevant entities: DNS service providers, TLD name registries, cloud computing, data centre and content delivery network providers, managed service and managed security service providers, online marketplaces, online search engines, social networking services platforms and trust service providers. Article 2 requires them to apply the technical and methodological cybersecurity risk-management measures in the Annex, proportionate to their risk exposure, size and incident likelihood and impact; where a requirement applies 'where appropriate', 'where applicable' or 'to the extent feasible' and is not applied, the entity must document its reasoning. The Annex covers policy, risk management, incident handling, business continuity, supply chain security, acquisition and development, security testing, cyber hygiene and training, cryptography, human resources, access control, asset management and physical security. Article 3 sets significance criteria, including direct financial loss above the lower of EUR 500 000 or 5% of turnover and severe operational disruption; Article 4 aggregates recurring incidents; Articles 5 to 14 add criteria per entity type based on outage durations and user shares. Article 15 repeals Regulation (EU) 2018/151. Binding and directly applicable in all Member States; enters into force on the twentieth day after OJ publication.

obligations.summary: Relevant entities (DNS service providers, TLD registries, cloud, data centre, CDN, managed and managed security service providers, online marketplaces, search engines, social networking platforms, trust service providers) must ensure a level of network and information system security appropriate to the risks, taking into account their exposure, size, incident likelihood and severity.
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall ensure a level of security of network and information systems appropriate to the risks posed

obligations.summary: Where a relevant entity considers a technical or methodological requirement with 'where appropriate', 'where applicable' or 'to the extent feasible' not appropriate, not applicable or not feasible, it must document its reasoning in a comprehensible manner.
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
obligations.conditional_on: where the entity considers a requirement not appropriate, not applicable or not feasible

evidence.quote: the relevant entity shall in a comprehensible manner document its reasoning to that effect

obligations.summary: Relevant entities must consider the listed categories when counting users impacted by an incident (customers with access contracts, and natural and legal persons associated with business customers), for the purposes of Articles 7 and 9 to 14.
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)
obligations.conditional_on: when counting users impacted by an incident

evidence.quote: the relevant entities shall consider all of the following

obligations.summary: Annex point 1: the policy on the security of network and information systems must set out the approach, objectives, commitments, roles, documentation, indicators and approval date listed in point 1.1.1, be reviewed at least annually, and responsibilities must be assigned to roles and reported to management bodies (points 1.1-1.2).
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: the policy on the security of network and information systems shall:

obligations.summary: Relevant entities must require all personnel and third parties to apply network and information system security in accordance with the established security policy and procedures (point 1.2.2).
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall require all personnel and third parties to apply network and information system security

obligations.summary: Annex point 2: relevant entities must establish and maintain a risk management framework, perform and document risk assessments, establish a risk treatment plan, follow a risk management process listed in point 2.1.2 and review it at least annually.
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall perform and document risk assessments

obligations.summary: Relevant entities must regularly review compliance with their security policies and operate an effective compliance reporting system to the management bodies (points 2.2.1-2.2.3).
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall regularly review the compliance with their policies on network and information system security

obligations.summary: Relevant entities must independently review their approach to network and information system security at planned intervals, through individuals with appropriate audit competence, with results reported to management bodies (points 2.3.1-2.3.4).
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall review independently their approach to managing network and information system security

obligations.summary: Relevant entities must establish and implement an incident handling policy covering detection, analysis, containment, response, recovery, documentation and reporting of incidents, coherent with the business continuity plan (points 3.1.1-3.1.3).
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: the relevant entities shall establish and implement an incident handling policy

obligations.summary: Relevant entities must monitor and log activity on their network and information systems, maintain, document and review logs, keep logs for a predefined period, and protect them from unauthorised access (points 3.2.1-3.2.7).
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: the relevant entities shall maintain, document, and review logs

obligations.summary: Relevant entities must put in place a simple mechanism for employees, suppliers and customers to report suspicious events, and train employees on its use (points 3.3.1-3.3.2).
obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall put in place a simple mechanism allowing their employees, suppliers, and customers to report suspicious events.

obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall assess suspicious events to determine whether they constitute incidents

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall establish communication plans and procedures

obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

evidence.quote: The relevant entities shall test at planned intervals their incident response procedures.

obligations.applies_from: from entry into force, the twentieth day following publication in the Official Journal (Art. 16)

enforcement.note: The Regulation sets technical and methodological requirements for cybersecurity risk-management measures (Art. 2, Annex) and criteria for significant incidents (Arts. 3-14), and contains no sanction, penalty or enforcement provisions. It is made under powers in Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (Art. 21(5), Art. 23(11)). Recital 36 mentions 'administrative fines' only to exclude them from the calculation of financial losses, which is not a sanction regime.
